title: A common blackbody area has a small fit cost in three 2023 ASASSN-14ko XMM spectra with a variable corona
abstract: We test whether the 2023 ASASSN-14ko X-ray dip requires loss of soft emitting area. We fit three EPIC-pn spectra with the published residual floor, a blackbody, and a power law with independent slope and strength in each observation. Blackbody normalization follows area times temperature to the fourth power. In 0.3-4.5 keV, one fitted common area increases W by 3.86 relative to three independent areas, with two fewer parameters. At the fixed reference area the later blackbody cools to the 25-eV fit bound while the coronal slope reaches 2.73. Cooling below the observed band leaves area weakly identified. This is a conditional null constraint, not evidence for cooling. Removing photons below 0.5 keV raises the fixed reference-area cost in the later spectrum from 2.47 to 9.82. The result depends on spectral family and energy band. It does not distinguish cooling with a changing corona, opaque covering, or loss of the inner flow. Code, input hashes, a retrieval recipe and aggregate fits are supplied.

display.caption: Conditional area profiles and fitted temperatures. One common area increases W by 3.86 in the primary model. A fit-bound temperature is not a measurement.
